thread:
jamie: 🚨 Seeing sustained p95/p99 latency regressions on /v1/generate since ~07:10 UTC. Pager went off, and we've got 3 support escalations from customers in EU and NA. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~920ms, p99 up to ~2.4s. Notable spike coincides with a model rollout at 07:05 by mike. Request IDs: req_8f3a, req_8f3b, req_8f4c.

alexa: oncall here — thanks. Are these synthetic or real user traces? Any commonalities (model, region, batch size)?

jamie: mixed. Observability: most errors are latency, not 5xx. Traces show long time in `queue.wait` and `model.decode`. Top affected route is `text-generation` with model variant `redwood-v2-1q`. Region: eu-west-1 and us-east-1.

mike: yeah, I rolled a kernel/quantization change for v2-1q at 07:04 to try to improve memory footprint. It passed perf tests locally but maybe altered runtime scheduling. Rolling back now. Triggering `deploy rollback redwood-v2-1q @ 1768004250`.

praveen: seeing backend cluster CPU pinned on some nodes in eu-west-1. Autoscaler didn't spin up additional nodes because we hit per-customer GPU quotas — dedicated pools are saturated.

ops-bot: Deploy rollback started for redwood-v2-1q (initiated by mike). Status: rollback_in_progress.

jamie: mitigation checklist I'm proposing: 1) rollback (in progress), 2) enable stricter per-customer rate-limits (soft) for 10m, 3) enable circuit-breaker to 95th token latency, 4) route traffic to fallback model `redwood-v2-1` in secondary region ap-southeast-1 for retriable requests, 5) notify customers. Thoughts?

alexa: +1 to rollback + rate-limits. For circuit-breaker, can we use token-latency based CB in the router? Need exact config.

mike: router supports CB with `latency_window_ms` and `failure_ratio`. Suggest: `latency_window_ms: 1200, failure_ratio: 0.20, sample_size: 1000`. That will open for paths where p95 > 1.2s. We should also set `fallback_model: redwood-v2-1` and `max_fallback_rate: 30%` so we don't overwhelm fallback.

jamie: adding commands for SRE runbook:

```
# temporary soft rate limit at router layer
route-config set /v1/generate --rate-limit 40rps --burst 80 --duration 10m

# enable circuit breaker
route-config set /v1/generate --circuit-breaker "latency_window_ms=1200,failure_ratio=0.2,sample_size=1000"

# fallback routing
route-config set /v1/generate --fallback "model=redwood-v2-1,region=ap-southeast-1,max_rate=0.3"
```

sarah: heads-up — I replied to the three escalations explaining we're investigating and offering temporary mitigation (fallback and reduced rates). Customer-facing msg: "We're rolling back a model change and applying temporary routing/rate-limits to stabilize latency; you may see slightly different output during the window."

praveen: I've opened a quota bump ticket for eu-west-1 to enable autoscale (internal req 5482). In the meantime I can tag a couple of warm nodes to accept spillover.

ops-bot: Deploy rollback status: success. Deployed version: redwood-v2-1 (prev stable). Time: 1768004380.

jamie: good — initial metrics post-rollback show p95 dropping to ~310ms after 2 minutes, p99 ~780ms. Still elevated vs baseline but trending down. We'll keep rate-limits in place until p99 < 600ms for 10 minutes.

alexa: can we add a brief guardrail in the API: return `x-rate-limit-reason: latency_guard` header when the soft limit triggers, and response code 429 for excess? That helps customers auto-backoff.

mike: yes — router patch applied: it will emit `X-Redwood-Guard: latency-circuit` and `X-Redwood-Fallback: redwood-v2-1` when activated. Example response snippet: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Guard: latency-circuit
Retry-After: 5
{
  "error": "requests temporarily limited due to latency mitigation"
}
```

jamie: ops checklist for closing incident: 
- Confirm p99 < 600ms for 10m (metric: api.latency.p99 /route=text-generation)
- Remove soft rate-limits gradually (stage: 80% -> 50% -> off)
- Keep circuit-breaker in monitoring but raise threshold back after 1h of stability
- Postmortem to include root cause (kernel/quant changes), telemetry gaps, and process change: require end-to-end canary with traffic shaping before model rollouts.

praveen: adding note: also track quota fallback policy. If dedicated pools are saturated, router should prefer fallback region models earlier rather than queue. New issue: INFRA-298 for smarter spillover.

sarah: I'll send a short templated update to customers in impacted orgs + support channels with the headers to look for.

alexa: final ask before I close oncall — can SRE add an automated playbook script that runs the above commands and posts to #support automatically? We should reduce manual steps.

mike: I can PR a playbook: `scripts/latency_mitigation.sh` with flags `--soft-rate --cb --fallback --notify`. Will include dry-run and required approvals.

jamie: thanks all. I'll keep monitoring and will post final stats once p99 sustained < 600ms. Marking incident in incidents channel and will create postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident incident-1768004321 created and linked to postmortem draft doc (incidents/1768004321).
